text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: reserved-pool-latency for tenant=aventus-health, severity=high, metric=tail_latency_p95 > 800ms

pagerduty: Incident P12345 created and routed to oncall schedule 'infra-oncall'.

Sanjay (oncall): acked. grabbing bridge. starting quick triage. any recent deploys to dedicated clusters?

Martina: no deploys in last 2 hours to that cluster. I see elevated queue length on reserved pool 'rsv-pool-7' linked to tenant aventus-health.

Maya: heartbeats look fine for nodes, but p95 token-serving latency is spiking and io wait is high on node-14.

Sanjay (oncall): good — let's snapshot: `curl -s http://metrics/api/query?m=tail_latency_p95{tenant="aventus-health"}` returned 920ms. KV cache miss rate jumped from 3% -> 28% in the last 3m.

Ryan: adding logs from runtime:
```
[2024-06-18T02:34:12Z] WARN tenant=aventus-health kvcache miss_rate=0.28 evictions=432 io_wait=0.34
[2024-06-18T02:34:18Z] ERROR tenant=aventus-health request_queue=120 backlog=4
```

Alex (support): customer impact — AventusHealth reports slower inference in prod UI for a segment of users. Support ticket #5892 open, they said some requests time out after 30s.

Sanjay (oncall): okay immediate mitigations: 1) enable burst-capacity on their reserved pool, 2) shift some weight to backup dedicated pool (fallback routing), 3) flush local kvcache on the hot nodes to avoid thrashing. Doing 1 & 2 now.

Martina: I'm triggering the rotation to backup pool: `redwoodctl pools rotate --from rsv-pool-7 --to rsv-pool-11 --tenant aventus-health --drain 30s`

ops-bot: Rotation request accepted. Jobs queued: rotate-1723456789-01.

Sanjay (oncall): fyi doing cache flush on node-14: `ssh node-14 sudo systemctl restart redwood-kvcache`

Maya: node-14 kvcache restart completed. miss_rate dropped to ~4% after restart. p95 reduced to 420ms.

Ryan: rotation job started, traffic reweighted by 30% to rsv-pool-11. Monitoring impact.

incident-bot: PagerDuty P12345 acknowledged by Sanjay (oncall). escalation timer paused.

Sanjay (oncall): good signal — p95 down to 310ms and request queue at 20. still higher than normal but improving. keeping bridge open.

Martina: root-cause hypothesis: kvcache thrash caused by a small group of chatty long-seq requests from AventusHealth that bypassed prefix cache and caused evictions. autoscaler didn't spin up extra capacity because pool was pinned to reserved capacity max.

Maya: I've opened a temporary policy tweak to allow burst-capacity up to +40% for this reserved pool: `redwoodctl pools update rsv-pool-7 --burst 40` — applied.

Alex (support): notified AventusHealth support lead (cc: ops) that we applied mitigations and are monitoring. asked them to throttle test traffic pattern if they can.

Ryan: added a quick canary rule to drop abnormally long sequences for that tenant at the ingress as a protective measure: `ingress.rule add --tenant aventus-health --if seq_len > 4096 --action slow-path` — pushing now.

Sanjay (oncall): metrics steady, p95 ~280ms, errors ~0.2% over baseline. I'll keep the bridge for 30 more mins then handoff to next oncall.

Martina: logged runbook steps and commands to incident ticket P12345. Suggested follow-ups: 1) investigate prefix caching behavior for tenant-scoped requests, 2) review reserved pool autoscaler config (min/max), 3) add a long-seq quota enforcement on reserved pools.

Maya: capturing heap profiles and kvcache histograms for node-14/15 and saving to s3 `s3://rdw-infra/incidents/P12345/` for postmortem.

ops-bot: Rotation job rotate-1723456789-01 completed successfully. rsv-pool-11 now serving 45% of AventusHealth traffic.

Sanjay (oncall): handing off to Martina for overnight monitoring. I'm out in 10. If latency creeps back above 600ms escalate to PD again.

Martina: taking handoff. setting reminder to re-evaluate in 15m and again hourly. updating ticket and tagging eng-runtime and platform teams for root cause.

Alex (support): I'll keep customer updated — told them we applied mitigations and will follow up with RCA.

incident-bot: PagerDuty P12345 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Sanjay (oncall): closing bridge for now. thanks team. :thumbsup:

Martina: noted next steps: postmortem draft to be started by eng-runtime, include metrics baseline, cache hit-rate delta, autoscaler config, and timeline. assigning to Maya (lead).

Maya: acknowledged. I'll start the PM and ping runtime for any kernel-level telemetry.

Ryan: leaving one action: add a synthetic test for long-seq traffic on reserved pools to surface kvcache thrash in staging.

Sanjay (oncall): all set. handoff complete.
